tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session loads a listing page with a 'Recent Comments' widget, identifies a sidebar link (dom index 67) that points to '/?p=8#comment-21', clicks it, and eventually ends up on the post URL with fragment '#comment-21'. A click sometimes opened an external author link (example.com) in another tab; therefore relying on clicks is brittle. Direct URL navigation is deterministic and avoids accidental external opens.

Task Definition:
- Create a deterministic, reusable tool that opens a referenced comment thread from the Recent Comments widget by navigating directly to the post URL with the comment fragment and verifying the comment is present. The tool must accept the site origin, post id (p), and the comment id as inputs.

Action Plan:
1. Construct the target URL using inputs: {site_base_url}/?p={p}#comment-{comment_id}.
2. Navigate to that URL (single navigation step) instead of clicking the sidebar link to avoid external-link mis-clicks.
3. Wait a short interval for the page and in-page anchor to load/scroll.
4. Extract/verify that an element with id 'comment-{comment_id}' exists and return author/snippet for confirmation.

Variable Identification:
- site_base_url (string): origin used to form the absolute URL. Extracted from session: "http://localhost:8000".
- p (string): post id in the query string; extracted value in session: "8".
- comment_id (string): numeric identifier used in the fragment; extracted value in session: "21".
- widget_selector (string, optional): CSS selector for the Recent Comments widget (e.g. "#recentcomments"), included for diagnostics but not required for navigation.

Step Optimization:
- Replace the UI click on the sidebar entry with a direct navigation step. This eliminates the risk of clicking a wrong anchor (author profile) and makes execution deterministic.
- Add a small static wait (2s) to reduce flakiness from transient load/scroll timing issues; the wait is conservative and short to keep the tool fast.
- Use an extraction step (extract_page_content) to confirm the comment anchor is present. This provides an explicit success signal rather than relying only on the URL fragment.
- Avoid agentic UI interactions unless the direct navigation fails; the tool is single-purpose and deterministic.

Notes and Rationale:
- The original attempt produced a transient navigation to example.com because clicking the author link in the widget can open external domains. Constructing the exact target URL from known parameters eliminates that error class.
- The widget_selector parameter is optional and only for diagnostics/advanced verification; the core operation does not require interacting with the widget DOM.

Constraints and Assumptions:
- The caller is already authenticated if the site requires auth; tool does not perform login.
- site_base_url must include scheme and host (e.g., "http://localhost:8000"). Do not include trailing path fragments.
- The target comment is reachable via a URL of the form '/?p={p}#comment-{comment_id}'. If the site uses a different permalink structure, the tool will need adjusted inputs.
name: open_recent_comment_target.v3
description: Open a specific comment thread referenced in the site's 'Recent Comments' widget by navigating directly to the post URL with the comment fragment and verifying the comment is present. Optimized to use direct navigation to the target URL (/{?p}#comment-{id}) instead of clicking sidebar links to avoid accidental external link clicks.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the post URL containing the comment fragment to open the referenced comment thread.
Wait a short time for page and in-page anchor scrolling to complete so the comment element is available in the DOM.
Check for the presence of the comment anchor and return structured data (presence flag, author name, comment snippet, post title).
steps.goal: Verify that an element with id 'comment-{comment_id}' exists on the page and extract the comment author and comment text for verification.

input_schema.name: site_base_url
input_schema.description: Base origin of the site, including scheme and host (e.g. "http://localhost:8000" or "https://example.com"). Do NOT include a trailing path. Required.

input_schema.name: p
input_schema.description: Post id used in the query parameter 'p' (example: "8"). This is used to construct the post URL '/?p={p}'. Required.

input_schema.name: comment_id
input_schema.description: Numeric comment id portion that will be appended to the fragment as '#comment-{comment_id}' (example: "21"). Required.

input_schema.name: widget_selector
input_schema.description: CSS selector for the Recent Comments widget container (used only for diagnostics). Default behaviour does not require it, but you can provide e.g. "#recentcomments" or ".widget_recent_comments".
